## The two papers

**Peters 1964**, *Gravitational radiation and the motion of two point masses.* Four pages, pure
analysis: how a binary's orbit decays as it radiates. Everything in the second half of the
lecture is this paper. It is from 1964 and short, which makes it an unusually honest
test of what a model knows against what it can look up.

**1608.01940**, *The basic physics of the binary black hole merger GW150914.* The opposite
approach: start from the strain data, read two numbers off a plot, and conclude that the objects
must be black holes. No relativity beyond what you saw in the lecture.

They meet in one place: the peak luminosity of GW150914 is exactly $-dE/dt$ from Peters'
circular orbital decay. One formula, arrived at from opposite ends, fifty years apart.
